literal: Than good company even greater support there is not; than bad company sorrow that which causes even there is not.
translation: There is no greater support than good company, and nothing causes more sorrow than bad company.
modern: நல்ல கூட்டத்தை விட சிறந்த துணை வேறு இல்லை. தீய கூட்டத்தை விட துன்பம் தருவது வேறு எதுவும் இல்லை.
explanation: This couplet contrasts the profound effects of good and bad company on a person's life. The word 'நல்லினம்' refers to a group of virtuous people, which acts as the greatest support ('துணை') one can have. Conversely, 'தீயினம்' means a group of wicked people, which is identified as the ultimate source of sorrow ('அல்லல்'). The poet uses a perfectly balanced parallel structure to emphasize that just as nothing helps you more than good friends, nothing harms you more than bad ones.
